question: If a medieval monk copied one page a day, how many years would it take to copy the whole Bible by hand?
explainer: A full Bible runs to about 1,200 printed pages. One page a day, every day, is about 3.3 years for a single copy.

question: How many cups of tea could have been brewed from all the tea dumped at the Boston Tea Party?
explainer: About 92,000 pounds of tea, roughly 42,000 kg, went into Boston Harbor in 1773. At 2 g a cup that is about 21 million cups.
source_title: Boston Tea Party facts and numbers (Boston Tea Party Historical Society)

question: How many years would it take to spend the Louisiana Purchase price of $15 million at $1,000 a day?
explainer: In 1803 the US paid $15 million for the Louisiana territory. At $1,000 a day that is 15,000 days, about 41 years.

question: How many human lifetimes ago did the last woolly mammoths die out?
explainer: The last mammoths, on Wrangel Island, died out about 4,000 years ago, while the pyramids already stood. That is only about 53 lifetimes back.

question: How many generations separate us from the fall of the Western Roman Empire in AD 476?
explainer: From 476 to 2026 is 1,550 years. At 25 years a generation that is about 62 generations: a line of 62 parents and children.
source_title: Fall of the Western Roman Empire (Wikipedia)

question: How many human lifetimes have passed since Rome was founded in 753 BC?
explainer: From 753 BC to 2026 is 2,779 years. Divided by 75, that is about 37 lifetimes end to end.

question: How many generations separate you from the first modern humans to leave Africa, about 60,000 years ago?
explainer: 60,000 years divided by 25 years a generation is about 2,400 generations of parents and children.

question: How many human lifetimes have passed since Leonardo painted the Mona Lisa in 1503?
explainer: From 1503 to 2026 is 523 years, which is about seven lifetimes laid end to end.

question: How many Olympic swimming pools of water did ancient Rome's aqueducts deliver every day?
explainer: Rome's eleven aqueducts are usually reckoned to have delivered about a million cubic metres a day for a city of about a million people. An Olympic pool holds 2,500 cubic metres, so about 400 pools a day.

question: If the whole history of modern humans were squeezed into one year, how many days ago did the first cities appear?
explainer: Our species is about 300,000 years old and the first cities, such as Uruk, appeared about 6,000 years ago: two percent of the way back, which on a one-year scale is the last seven days.
source_title: The first of our kind: Jebel Irhoud - Max Planck Society

question: How many Manhattans would fit inside the land of the Louisiana Purchase?
explainer: The Louisiana Purchase of 1803 covered about 2.14 million square kilometres. Manhattan is 59 square kilometres, so about 36,000 Manhattans would fit.

question: Walking all day, every day, how many years would it take to walk every section of the Great Wall of China?
explainer: China's survey measured 21,196 km of wall. At 25 km a day that is 848 days, about 2.3 years.

question: How many Titanics would it take to equal the weight of the Great Pyramid of Giza?
explainer: The Great Pyramid weighs about 5.9 million tonnes and the Titanic displaced about 52,000 tonnes, so about 110 Titanics.

question: How many human lifetimes fit between the building of the Great Pyramid and today?
explainer: The Great Pyramid was finished around 2560 BC, about 4,570 years ago. Divided by a 75-year life, that is only about 61 lifetimes end to end.

question: How many Olympic swimming pools would the stone of the Great Pyramid fill?
explainer: The pyramid's volume is about 2.6 million m³. An Olympic pool holds 2,500 m³, so about 1,000 pools of solid stone.

question: Counting out loud at one person a second, how many years would it take to count everyone who has ever lived?
source_title: How many people have ever lived on Earth? (PRB)
explainer: About 117 billion people have ever been born. At one a second, with 31.6 million seconds in a year, that is about 3,700 years.

question: How many times faster is a modern airliner than the Wright brothers' first flight in 1903?
explainer: The Wright Flyer's first hop averaged about 10.9 km/h. A jet cruises at about 900 km/h, roughly 83 times faster.

question: Walking all day, every day, how many years would it take to walk every road the Romans ever built?
source_title: New map transforms what we know about Roman roads (Scientific American)
explainer: A 2025 map puts the Roman road network at about 300,000 km. At 30 km a day that is 10,000 days, about 27 years of walking.

question: How many gold wedding rings could be made from Tutankhamun's solid gold coffin?
explainer: Tutankhamun's innermost coffin is about 110 kg of gold, which is 110,000 g. At 5 g a ring that is about 22,000 wedding rings.

question: To finish the Great Pyramid in 20 years, how many stone blocks did its builders have to set every day?
explainer: The pyramid has about 2.3 million blocks. Over 20 years, 7,305 days, that is about 315 blocks a day: one every few minutes, day and night.

question: If everything since the Great Pyramid was built were squeezed into one 24-hour day, how many minutes would the World Wide Web have existed?
explainer: The pyramid is about 4,570 years old and the Web went public in 1991, about 35 years ago. 35 ÷ 4,570 of a 1,440-minute day is about 11 minutes.

question: Building one kilometre a week, how many years would it take to build every section of the Great Wall of China?
explainer: There are 21,196 km of wall and 52 weeks in a year, so about 410 years at a kilometre a week.

question: If the Great Pyramid's stone blocks were laid in a single line, how many kilometres would it stretch?
explainer: The pyramid has about 2.3 million blocks averaging about 1.3 m across. In a line that is 3 million metres, about 3,000 km: Cairo to London.

question: How many Londons of the year 1600 would fit into today's London, by population?
explainer: London had about 200,000 people in 1600 and about 8.9 million today, so today's city is about 45 Shakespeare-era Londons.

question: If you spent one minute in every year since the Great Pyramid was built, how many days would that take?
explainer: The pyramid is about 4,570 years old. 4,570 minutes is 76 hours, about 3.2 days.

question: How many people could stand on the arena floor of the Colosseum, four to a square metre?
explainer: The arena floor was an oval about 76 m by 44 m, roughly 2,600 square metres. At four people to a square metre, about 10,500 people could pack onto it.

question: The US paid $15 million for the Louisiana Purchase in 1803. How many cents was that per acre?
explainer: The Purchase covered about 2.14 million square kilometres, which is about 530 million acres. Fifteen million dollars spread over that is under three cents an acre.

question: How many bath towels could be cut from the cloth of the Bayeux Tapestry?
explainer: The Bayeux Tapestry is nearly 70 m long and about 50 cm wide, around 34 square metres of linen. A bath towel is about 70 cm by 140 cm, so you could cut about 35 of them.

question: How many double beds would it take to cover the floor of the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles?
source_title: Palace of Versailles: Hall of Mirrors - Bluffton University
explainer: The Hall of Mirrors is 73 m long and 10.5 m wide, about 770 square metres. A double bed is about 1.4 m by 1.9 m, so roughly 290 beds would carpet it.

question: Rome's aqueducts brought in about a million cubic metres of water a day. How many bathtubs was that for each Roman, every day?
explainer: Ancient Rome had about a million people, so a million cubic metres a day is about 1,000 litres each: more than three 300-litre bathtubs per Roman, every day.

question: At a camel caravan's pace, how many months would it take to travel the Silk Road from Xi’an to the Mediterranean?
explainer: The Silk Road ran about 6,400 km from Xi’an to the Mediterranean. A laden camel caravan covered roughly 30 km a day, so the whole way took about 210 days, around seven months.

question: How many times longer have modern humans been around than the Great Pyramid has stood?
source_title: The first of our kind: Jebel Irhoud - Max Planck Society
explainer: Our species goes back about 300,000 years, to the Jebel Irhoud fossils, while the Great Pyramid was finished around 2560 BC, about 4,600 years ago. So humans have been around about 65 times longer than the pyramid.
